name: World Health Assembly adopts stroke resolution
headline: World Health Assembly approves its first resolution on stroke
summary: On 22 May 2026 delegates at the Seventy-ninth World Health Assembly approved the Assembly's first-ever resolution on stroke.
keyPoints: Delegates approved the resolution on 22 May 2026, according to the WHO's daily update from the Seventy-ninth World Health Assembly.
It is titled "Reducing the burden of stroke: strengthening prevention, acute care, rehabilitation and health-system readiness".
The WHO update says the lifetime risk of stroke has risen by 50% over the past 20 years and that 1 in 4 adults is expected to have a stroke in their lifetime.
The resolution calls for stronger national and global action on prevention, acute care, rehabilitation and health-system readiness.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: On 22 May 2026 delegates at the Seventy-ninth World Health Assembly, the decision-making meeting of the World Health Organization (WHO), approved the Assembly's first-ever resolution on stroke. The resolution is titled "Reducing the burden of stroke: strengthening prevention, acute care, rehabilitation and health-system readiness". It was proposed by Egypt and co-sponsored by Chile, Georgia, Palestine, Paraguay and Tunisia.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The WHO's update says the lifetime risk of stroke has risen by 50% over the past 20 years and that 1 in 4 adults is expected to have a stroke in their lifetime. The resolution calls for stronger national and global action on prevention, acute care, rehabilitation and health-system readiness.
